subject: Tenant data custody & inference assertions — operational roadmap
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@helixhealth.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: alaa@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant custody / training exclusion questions for DPA

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and routing controls. Before we proceed to procurement, legal asked for clarity on two items in the DPA you shared:

1) A firm commitment that Helix tenant inputs and generated responses will never be used to improve public models (we need explicit "no-training" or "no-model-improvement" language).
2) Who the subprocessors are for inference/eval pipelines and whether any of them can export model artifacts cross-border; we need onshore residency for EU patient data and a proof-of-process for any transfers.

I've attached our standard DPA template with the sections highlighted. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the no-training clause as written or propose a narrow operational carveout? Also please advise what evidence you can provide for subprocessor controls.

Appreciate a short timeline — procurement would like to close by end of month.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Compliance
Helix Health

[Attachment: Helix_DPA_draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 124KB)]

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Tenant custody / training exclusion questions for DPA

Team — forwarding Helix's asks. High-level thoughts: we can commit to a contractual operational "no-training" promise for Helix tenant data with the right controls (ephemeral KV + explicit exclude flag + onshore-only subprocessor lane). Legal will need to craft the language so it ties to specific operational constraints (e.g., disable model-improvement pipelines for HX account id, provide attestation).

Specific asks for follow-up:
- David: propose DPA language that maps to the operational knobs (no-training, derivative ownership, audit evidence).
- Kimberly: confirm subprocessor inventory and whether we can promise onshore-only processing for EU patient PII and provide a proof-of-process (SFTP/airgap or dedicated VPC routing).
- Marissa: commercial impact — will Helix expect discounts for a dedicated onshore lane or reserved capacity? Need a quick estimate.

Timeline: Marta says procurement wants close by 3/31. Can we turn a redline by EOD?

Thanks,
Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: david.kim@redwood.com
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tenant custody / training exclusion questions for DPA

Team — attaching a redline with suggested language that: (a) defines "no-model-improvement" as "no use of customer inputs or outputs to update model weights or produce derivative training datasets;" (b) clarifies that telemetry and anonymized usage metrics required for billing/performance will be separated and cannot be used for model training; (c) commits to quarterly attestation and an evidence bundle for subprocessors.

Operational caveat to capture: the promise is conditional on the customer enabling the account-level opt-out flag and using supported ingestion paths (API header X-Redwood-NoTrain: true) — we can't enforce opt-out on legacy SFTP ingestion without additional gating. I've included an appendix describing acceptable evidence (subprocessor attestations, onshore routing logs, redacted KV cache snapshots).

Attachment: RDW_DPA_redline_jd_20280319.docx (redline; legal comments inline)

David
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@helixhealth.com>, Alaa Rahman <alaa@helixhealth.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant custody / training exclusion questions for DPA

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear asks and the DPA draft. Quick summary of what we can offer and next steps: 

1) No-training commitment: Redwood will add a contractual clause that Helix tenant data (inputs and generated responses) will not be used to improve model weights or to create training datasets for any public or internal model, provided Helix enables the account-level opt-out and uses supported ingestion paths (API with header or Dedicated/VPC connectors). We cannot retroactively guarantee the same for bulk legacy ingestion methods unless routed through the opt-out lane.

2) Subprocessors & residency: Kimberly confirms the inference chain uses two primary subprocessors for GPU hosting and observability. We can map Helix traffic to an onshore-only pool for EU patient data (onshore lane) and provide a subprocessor attestation package (SOC-like checklist + export control audits).

3) Evidence: Legal will produce a quarterly attestation and a one-time evidence bundle (subprocessor roster, redacted logs showing onshore routing, and a short operational runbook for the opt-out flag).

4) Commercial: Marissa — there may be a modest premium for a committed onshore lane or reserved capacity; we'll put numbers in a separate note.

Next steps: I attached David's redline. Can you review and confirm whether the opt-out gating approach and evidence package meet Helix's procurement requirements? If yes, we'll circulate the final redline for signature by 3/29.

Link to draft folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Helix-DPA

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RDW_DPA_redline_jd_20280319.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@helixhealth.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: alaa@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant custody / training exclusion questions for DPA

Jasmine — this is helpful, thank you. A few quick notes from our side: 

• The opt-out gating is acceptable so long as the DPA explicitly requires Redwood to provide the quarter attestation and the initial evidence bundle before go-live.
• For EU patient data we will need the onshore lane documented and a short runbook we can hand to our security team. Please include timelines for delivering evidence (we'd prefer evidence within 5 business days of request).
• Commercial: procurement will likely ask for a small credit given the additional operational controls; we'll circle back after we see Marissa's estimate.

If you can turn the final redline by 3/27 we can route for signature the following week. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Best,
Marta
Head of Compliance, Helix Health
